title: Microsoft scales down plans for Mount Pleasant data center
source_used: Construction Review (In Business Madison read as well)
key_facts: Microsoft proposes to replace nine planned data-center buildings at its Durand Avenue campus in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, with seven single-story data centers, a storage building and two utility substations, according to documents submitted to the village.
The revised plan would increase total proposed floor area by about 400,000 square feet, to 5,878,080 square feet.
The village Plan Commission reviews it at 1 p.m. on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026; village staff recommend approval; it had not been approved as of 12 Oct.
The proposal would cut the estimated taxable value per acre by about $2.3 million, to $7.7 million.
The village has approved plans for up to 15 data centers across two Microsoft campuses; the first Mount Pleasant data center is operational and a second is due in 2028.

In Business Madison, citing the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, calls it a scale-down with 'fewer buildings and less square footage', which conflicts with the floor-area increase reported by Construction Review.
Microsoft said the changes 'in no way reflect a reduction in our ambition' and were made for faster development.

event_date: Revised plan filed with the village before 12 Oct 2026; Plan Commission review 14 Oct 2026
notes: CONFLICT between sources: In Business Madison (the pool item) says 'less square footage'; Construction Review, citing the filing, reports floor area up about 400,000 sq ft, and The Daily Reporter headline (blocked) also says 'larger footprint'. Used Construction Review for the numbers. Plan first reported 12 Oct, so score lowered for age and for the overstated 'scales down' headline.
